model-context-protocol.name: Model Context Protocol
model-context-protocol.explanation: An open protocol that lets AI apps call tools provided by separate programs. A server describes its tools (name, description, input schema); the client, here the agent, decides when to call them and gets structured results back.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: It's how any agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) can use the same diagramming tools without custom integrations.

json-rpc-over-stdio.name: JSON-RPC over stdio
json-rpc-over-stdio.explanation: The client starts the server as a child process and they exchange JSON-RPC messages over its standard input and output. No network port or HTTP server is needed.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: The server runs locally next to the repository, so stdio keeps it private and needs no setup beyond npx.

tty-detection.name: TTY detection
tty-detection.explanation: process.stdin.isTTY tells a program whether a person is typing at a terminal or another program is piping data in.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: One binary is both the MCP server (piped stdin) and a CLI; at a terminal it shows help instead of silently waiting.

agents-md.name: AGENTS.md instructions
agents-md.explanation: A Markdown file at the repository root that coding agents read for project instructions. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, which can import it with @AGENTS.md.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: The MCP server can't run on its own after a commit; the instruction file is what tells the agent to call it.

idempotent-upsert.name: Idempotent marker-block upsert
idempotent-upsert.explanation: Write generated text between start/end markers, and replace only that block on later runs. Running setup twice gives the same file, and everything outside the markers is left alone.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: init edits AGENTS.md and the post-commit hook, files that already belong to the user.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: .concepts.local.json is added to .gitignore only when no matching line exists.

git-hooks.name: Git hooks
git-hooks.explanation: Scripts git runs at points in its workflow. post-commit runs after every commit and can't block it.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: The hook prints a reminder that a commit is waiting; its output also reaches an agent that ran git commit.

git-plumbing.name: git rev-list and show
git-plumbing.explanation: Low-level git commands that scripts use: rev-list prints commit ids in a range, and show prints one commit's metadata, file stats or patch in a format you choose.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: They list commits since setup and extract each diff without depending on any git library.

processed-set.name: Watermark + processed set
processed-set.explanation: Remember where you started (a watermark) and which items are done, then compute the work left as 'everything after the watermark minus what's done'. Nothing is missed and nothing is done twice, however irregularly the job runs.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: Agents don't run after every commit, so the server works out what's pending from git history instead of trusting the last commit.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: A new or moved folder is seeded with the processed commits from an existing one, and pending work is the union across folders, so nothing is redone.

diff-budgeting.name: Context budgeting
diff-budgeting.explanation: Fit what you send a language model into a size limit on purpose: drop low-value content and share the remaining space fairly instead of cutting off at an arbitrary point.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: Lockfiles and generated files are removed and each changed file gets a fair share of the diff budget.

schema-validation.name: Schema validation with Zod
schema-validation.explanation: Describe the expected shape of data once and check untrusted input against it at runtime, getting precise errors back. MCP tool schemas are generated from the same definitions.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: Everything the agent sends is checked before any file is written, including links and file-name ids.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: requestState comes back through the client, so earlier answers are re-validated with a Zod schema before setup uses them.

path-traversal.name: Path traversal prevention
path-traversal.explanation: If user-supplied text becomes part of a file path, values like ../../ can escape the intended folder. Restricting ids to a safe pattern closes that hole.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: Concept ids become note file names, so they must match a lowercase slug pattern.

layered-graph-layout.name: Layered graph layout
layered-graph-layout.explanation: The Sugiyama method draws directed graphs in layers: assign nodes to ranks, reorder each rank to reduce crossing edges, then set coordinates. dagre implements it.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: The agent only says what connects to what; dagre decides where every box goes.

rough-js.name: Hand-drawn rendering with Rough.js
rough-js.explanation: Rough.js turns shapes into slightly wobbly, sketch-like strokes. It is the library behind Excalidraw's look and can output SVG paths without a browser.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: The SVG preview matches the Excalidraw file's style and renders on GitHub.

deterministic-ids.name: Deterministic ids from hashes
deterministic-ids.explanation: Derive ids and random seeds by hashing stable input instead of generating random ones, so the same input always produces byte-identical output.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: Re-rendering a commit produces the same .excalidraw file, so git diffs stay clean.

font-subsetting.name: Font subsetting
font-subsetting.explanation: Strip a font down to the characters you need so it is small enough to embed. Fonts under the SIL Open Font License must be renamed when modified if they have a reserved name.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: A Latin subset of Virgil is embedded in every SVG so the hand-drawn text shows on GitHub, renamed Concepts Hand.

atomic-write.name: Atomic file writes
atomic-write.explanation: Write to a temporary file, then rename it over the real one. A rename is atomic, so a crash leaves either the old file or the new one, never half of each.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: state.json is the record of what's been processed; a torn write would lose it.

npm-bin-npx.name: npx and package bin
npm-bin-npx.explanation: A package's bin field names the command it provides. npx downloads the package if needed and runs that command, so users never install anything globally.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: Every agent's MCP config is just `npx -y concepts-mcp@latest`.

trusted-publishing.name: npm trusted publishing (OIDC)
trusted-publishing.explanation: Instead of storing a long-lived npm token as a secret, the CI job proves its identity with a short-lived OpenID Connect token that npm trusts for this repository and workflow, and npm records provenance.

sightings.title: concepts-mcp: an MCP server that draws commits
sightings.whyHere: Releases publish from a tag with no secret to leak.

intermediate-representation.name: Intermediate representation
intermediate-representation.explanation: A neutral in-between format that one stage produces and several back ends consume, like a compiler's IR. Each back end only needs to understand the simple format, not the stage before it.

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: Layout emits a flat list of rectangles, ellipses, lines, arrows and text; the Excalidraw and SVG writers both draw exactly that list, so they can't drift apart.

discriminated-union.name: Discriminated unions
discriminated-union.explanation: A type that is one of several shapes, told apart by a tag field. Checking the tag tells you which fields exist, so validation and code can branch safely.

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: A view's `type` decides whether it has nodes and edges or participants and messages; Zod validates each branch with its own schema.

uml-diagrams.name: System-design diagram types
uml-diagrams.explanation: Standard ways to draw software: architecture (components and connections), sequence (messages over time), flowchart (steps and decisions), state machine (states and transitions) and data model (entities and relationships). Each answers a different question about a system.

learnMore.title: The C4 model for software architecture

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: Picking the right view for a change is what makes the diagram teach instead of just listing words.

compound-graph-layout.name: Compound graph layout
compound-graph-layout.explanation: Graph layout where some nodes contain others (clusters), so members are placed together and their boundary can be drawn around them.

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: Boundaries such as services, layers or trust zones are dagre clusters, so their members are laid out side by side.

sequence-layout.name: Sequence diagram layout
sequence-layout.explanation: Participants sit in columns with a dashed lifeline below each; time runs downward, one row per message. It needs no graph algorithm, just columns and rows.

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: Sequence views can't use the graph layout: their order is the point, so they get their own simple grid.

referential-integrity.name: Referential integrity checks
referential-integrity.explanation: When records point at each other by id, check every reference resolves before accepting the data, the way a database enforces foreign keys.

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: Edges must name nodes in their view, nodes must name real groups, and every appearsIn must name a real part; ids must be unique across views.

visual-encoding.name: Visual encoding
visual-encoding.explanation: Map each kind of information to a visual property people read at a glance (shape, color, line weight, dash) and use it consistently, with a key.

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: Shape says what a part is, fill color its role, outline weight whether this commit added it, dashes whether a message is async, and red numbers mark concepts.

excalidraw-scene-format.name: Excalidraw scene format
excalidraw-scene-format.explanation: An .excalidraw file is JSON: a list of elements (shapes, arrows, text, frames) with positions and style. Text can be bound to a container, arrows bound to the shapes they connect, and elements placed inside frames.

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: Each view becomes a frame; bindings are written both ways so the diagram stays connected when you edit it.

invariant-testing.name: Invariant-based tests
invariant-testing.explanation: Instead of comparing output to a saved picture, assert properties that must always hold, such as no overlapping boxes, every part inside its frame, every reference bound both ways. They survive harmless layout changes.

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: Layout output changes whenever spacing is tuned; the tests check what must stay true.

source-available-license.name: Source-available licensing
source-available-license.explanation: Publishing code people can read, use and modify while limiting some uses. PolyForm Noncommercial allows noncommercial use and changes but forbids commercial use; unlike open-source licenses such as MIT, it restricts who may use it.

sightings.title: Diagrams become system-design models
sightings.whyHere: The project switched from MIT so nobody can sell it.

aabb-intersection.name: Bounding-box intersection
aabb-intersection.explanation: Two axis-aligned rectangles overlap only if they overlap on both the x axis and the y axis. The overlap on each axis is min(right edges) − max(left edges).

sightings.title: Making room between boundaries
sightings.whyHere: It detects colliding boundaries, and the smaller of the two overlaps is the cheapest direction to push them apart.

space-insertion.name: Overlap removal by inserting space
space-insertion.explanation: To separate two things without wrecking a layout, draw a line between them and move everything beyond the line by the same amount. Relative order is kept, so the picture only stretches.

sightings.title: Making room between boundaries
sightings.whyHere: Parts, edge routes and labels past the cut all move together; each arrow's ends follow their own node so arrows stay attached.

fixed-point-iteration.name: Iterate until stable
fixed-point-iteration.explanation: Repeat a fixing step until a pass changes nothing, with a cap on passes so it always ends. Fixing one problem can create another, so a single pass isn't enough.

sightings.title: Making room between boundaries
sightings.whyHere: Opening one gap can make other boxes collide, so the check runs again, at most 40 times.

derived-state.name: Derived vs stored state
derived-state.explanation: If a value can be computed cheaply from data you already have, compute it when needed instead of saving it. Stored copies can go stale and every write has side effects.

sightings.title: Breaking a commit feedback loop
sightings.whyHere: Whether a commit only touched setup files is a fact about the commit, so it is now recomputed on every call.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: Former output folders aren't stored anywhere new: they're derived from the elsewhere field of seeded commits, so commits that only touch them are still skipped.

feedback-loop.name: Self-triggering feedback loops
feedback-loop.explanation: A process whose output becomes its own next input never settles. A common case is a tool that writes into the repository it is watching.

sightings.title: Breaking a commit feedback loop
sightings.whyHere: Recording a skip changed a tracked file, which needed a commit, which the tool then saw as new.

progressive-enhancement.name: Progressive enhancement
progressive-enhancement.explanation: Ship a page that already works as plain HTML, then let JavaScript add extras on top. If the script fails or is blocked, the visitor still gets the core content.

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: The library page lists the known diagrams in its HTML and only uses the script to add newer ones from state.json, so it never shows an empty grid.

static-json-as-api.name: A static file as a data API
static-json-as-api.explanation: A static site has no server code, but it can still fetch JSON files hosted next to it. A file the build or a tool keeps up to date becomes a read-only API.

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: concepts-mcp already writes state.json for every diagram, so the page reads it directly instead of needing a backend or a rebuild.

dedupe-by-key.name: Merging by a unique key
dedupe-by-key.explanation: When combining two lists that may overlap, index one by a unique key and only add items from the other whose key isn't there yet.

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: Cards in the HTML carry data-sha; the script collects those and adds only commits with an unseen short SHA, so nothing appears twice.

script-defer.name: Deferred scripts
script-defer.explanation: A <script defer> downloads in parallel with parsing and runs after the HTML is parsed, in order. It doesn't block rendering and can safely query the finished DOM.

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: library.js needs the grid and the existing cards to be in the DOM before it looks for them.

self-hosted-webfonts.name: Self-hosted web fonts
self-hosted-webfonts.explanation: Serving fonts from your own site with @font-face instead of a font CDN: no third-party requests, no tracking, and it works offline. WOFF2 is the compressed format browsers prefer; font-display: swap shows fallback text until the font loads.

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: The site loads Manrope, DM Sans and DM Mono from docs/assets/fonts with font-display: swap, keeping visitors' requests on GitHub Pages.

variable-fonts.name: Variable fonts
variable-fonts.explanation: One font file that contains a continuous range of weights (or other axes). @font-face declares the range, e.g. font-weight: 200 800, and the browser picks any weight in it.

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: Manrope and DM Sans each ship as one variable file instead of a file per weight, which keeps the download small.

css-custom-properties.name: CSS custom properties as design tokens
css-custom-properties.explanation: Variables declared in CSS (--ink: #17181f) and read with var(--ink). Defining colors and spacing once on :root keeps a design consistent and easy to change.

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: The new violet accent, ink, line and background colors are tokens that every component reuses.

fluid-typography.name: Fluid type with clamp()
fluid-typography.explanation: clamp(min, preferred, max) lets a size grow with the viewport (e.g. 7vw) but never go below or above set limits, replacing several media-query breakpoints.

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: The hero headline uses clamp(44px, 7vw, 78px) so it scales smoothly from phones to wide screens.

github-issue-forms.name: GitHub issue forms
github-issue-forms.explanation: YAML files in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE that turn a new issue into a form with labeled fields, dropdowns and required inputs, so reports arrive with the details maintainers need.

learnMore.title: GitHub Docs: Syntax for issue forms

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: Bug reports ask what happened, the agent and versions, and invite a screenshot of a broken diagram.

security-policy.name: Security policy (SECURITY.md)
security-policy.explanation: A file that tells people how to report a vulnerability privately instead of opening a public issue. GitHub links it from the repo's Security tab.

sightings.title: A redesigned site with a live library page
sightings.whyHere: An MCP server runs on users' machines and reads their repositories, so a private reporting path matters.

shell-glob-expansion.name: Shell glob expansion
shell-glob-expansion.explanation: In a Unix shell, an unquoted pattern like test/*.test.js is replaced by the matching file names before the program runs. Quoting it passes the pattern through unchanged, and then the program itself has to understand globs.

sightings.title: Listing test files so Node 20 finds them
sightings.whyHere: The quotes were there so Node's runner would expand the glob, which only Node 21+ does.

node-test-runner.name: Node's built-in test runner
node-test-runner.explanation: node --test runs test files with node:test and node:assert, without a framework. Its features vary by Node version: glob patterns as arguments arrived in Node 21.

sightings.title: Listing test files so Node 20 finds them
sightings.whyHere: The package supports Node 20+, so the script has to work with Node 20's runner too.

ci-version-matrix.name: CI version matrix
ci-version-matrix.explanation: Running the same CI job on several runtime versions at once, so a feature missing from the oldest supported version breaks the build instead of a user's install.

sightings.title: Listing test files so Node 20 finds them
sightings.whyHere: The Node 20 jobs in the matrix were what caught that the tests silently never ran there.

mcp-elicitation.name: MCP elicitation
mcp-elicitation.explanation: An MCP server can ask the user for structured input through the client: it sends a message plus a small JSON Schema (strings, numbers, booleans, enums), and the client shows a native form and returns accept, decline or cancel.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: setup_concepts shows the where and level pickers as forms in the agent's own UI instead of relying on the model to phrase the question.

multi-round-trip-requests.name: Multi-round-trip requests
multi-round-trip-requests.explanation: Instead of the server calling back into the client mid-request, a handler returns 'input required' with the questions and an opaque requestState. The client gathers the answers and retries the same call with them, so the server can stay stateless between rounds.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: Each round only brings back the latest answers, so earlier ones (where, levels) ride along in requestState until setup has everything.

capability-negotiation.name: Capability negotiation
capability-negotiation.explanation: At connection (or per request) the client declares which optional features it supports. A server checks those capabilities before using a feature, rather than finding out from an error.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: The server reads the client's elicitation capability (from the request envelope or the initialize handshake) to decide between a form and the fallback.

graceful-degradation.name: Graceful degradation
graceful-degradation.explanation: When a richer feature isn't available, fall back to a simpler path that still gets the job done instead of failing.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: Clients without forms get needsChoices with the same questions, and the agent asks them with its own multiple-choice tool.

single-source-of-truth.name: Single source of truth
single-source-of-truth.explanation: Define each piece of knowledge in one place and derive every other use from it, so copies can't drift apart.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: The options, their order, descriptions and the recommended default live in choices.js; the terminal picker, MCP form and agent questions all read it.

raw-mode-terminal.name: Raw-mode terminal input
raw-mode-terminal.explanation: A terminal normally buffers input until Enter. setRawMode(true) delivers each key immediately, and readline.emitKeypressEvents turns byte sequences like ESC [ B into named keys such as 'down'. Raw mode must be switched off again, even on Ctrl-C.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: The arrow-key pickers need single keypresses without adding a prompt library.

ansi-escape-redraw.name: Redrawing with ANSI escape codes
ansi-escape-redraw.explanation: Escape sequences such as ESC[3A (cursor up 3 lines) and ESC[J (clear to end of screen) let a program redraw part of the terminal in place. It only works if you know exactly how many rows you drew, so lines must never wrap.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: Each keypress redraws the picker in place, and rows are trimmed to the terminal width so a wrapped line can't break the redraw.

fake-stream-testing.name: Testing with fake streams
fake-stream-testing.explanation: Code that reads from stdin and writes to stdout can take the streams as parameters; tests pass in-memory PassThrough streams and write key sequences into them.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: The picker tests type arrow keys, digits, Space and Enter into a PassThrough instead of needing a real terminal.

layered-config.name: Layered config with a local override
layered-config.explanation: A committed config holds the team default; a personal, gitignored file on top of it can override parts of it for one person, like .env.local or settings.local.json.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: One teammate can save only to their Desktop library with every file while the repo keeps the shared, lighter setting.

migration-on-read.name: Schema migration on read
migration-on-read.explanation: Version the stored format and convert old versions to the new shape as they're read, writing the new version only when something changes. Old files keep working without a migration step.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: A version 1 .concepts.json becomes one destination that keeps writing every file, so upgrading changes nothing until settings change.

recommended-defaults.name: Recommended defaults
recommended-defaults.explanation: Offer a few clear choices, mark one as recommended and preselect it, so pressing Enter (or --yes) gives a good result and more options stay one step away.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: Every picker lists the simplest option first (Diagram, This project) and preselects it; Custom is there for people who want more.

git-generation-number.name: Ordering commits by history position
git-generation-number.explanation: git rev-list --count <sha> counts the commits reachable from a commit. A commit always counts higher than every ancestor, so the number orders commits by history even when timestamps tie, are rebased or come from skewed clocks.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: Several commits a day had sorted by random hash; the count now prefixes folders and orders the index.

zero-padded-sort-keys.name: Zero-padded sort keys
zero-padded-sort-keys.explanation: File browsers sort names as text, where '10' comes before '9'. Padding numbers to a fixed width ('00009', '00010') makes text order match number order.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: Commit folders start with a 5-digit sequence number so they list in commit order anywhere.

fan-out-writes.name: Fan-out to several outputs
fan-out-writes.explanation: One input is processed once and written to several destinations, each with its own options.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: One record_commit_concepts call writes to every configured folder at that folder's level, each with its own state and index.

aria-pressed-toggles.name: Toggle buttons with aria-pressed
aria-pressed-toggles.explanation: A button that stays on or off announces its state to screen readers through aria-pressed="true"/"false"; CSS can style the pressed state from the same attribute.

sightings.title: Choosing how much each commit saves, and where
sightings.whyHere: The website's Where and Detail pickers are groups of toggle buttons that also drive the init command shown.

cross-platform-paths.name: Cross-platform path separators
cross-platform-paths.explanation: Windows separates path parts with \ and macOS/Linux with /. Node's path module uses the current platform's separator (path.sep), so the same code produces different strings on each OS. Paths shown to people or compared in tests are often normalized to / first.

sightings.title: Showing folders the way people read them
sightings.whyHere: Project folders are now shown as repo-relative paths joined with /, so messages read the same everywhere and the Windows CI jobs pass.

display-vs-data.name: Display values vs data values
display-vs-data.explanation: Keep the precise value for programs (an absolute path) and derive a separate, friendlier form for people (docs/concepts, ~/ConceptLibrary). Formatting for display shouldn't change the data other code relies on.

sightings.title: Showing folders the way people read them
sightings.whyHere: The structured result still carries absolute paths; only the messages use the shown form.
